ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base is a power company that installs a battery at your home. Most homeowners have never heard of that, and most don’t like their electric utility. That’s our growth challenge. A homeowner has to understand a new kind of product, trust a company they just met, and finish an onboarding journey to get a battery installed. Every step is a chance to earn them or lose them.

Base is growing fast, in Texas and nationwide. We’re hiring a full stack engineer to own the products and systems that drive acquisition (getting found), activation (going from sign-up to a working battery) and retention (staying with Base and telling neighbors). That means 1) experimenting on and scaling our existing product, and 2) building new growth products and infrastructure from scratch.

Judgment is a core part of the job: knowing where to create leverage, which friction matters and which problems are worth solving. We care about conversion, but never at the expense of clarity, trust or the long-term quality of the brand.

This is a lean team that moves fast and gives you real ownership. We’re not looking for someone to execute a handed-down roadmap. We want someone who finds the opportunities, works from first principles and ships.



What You’ll Do

 - Turn ideas into shipped tests across the member journey, from redesigned sign-up flows to paid ads campaigns and referral experiences

 - Write the code, read the results and decide what to test next

 - Own the products and systems that drive acquisition, activation and retention

 - Build the growth infrastructure that makes experimentation fast and trustworthy, including the data pipeline behind it

 - Use judgment on where to create leverage and which problems are worth solving, optimizing for conversion without sacrificing clarity or trust

 - Find opportunities and work from first principles rather than executing a handed-down roadmap



What You’ll Bring

 - 2+ years of experience building production software in product or full-stack engineering roles

 - Strong frontend and full-stack engineering skills, with comfort across modern web applications, APIs, data models, and stateful user experiences.

 - Strong product judgment and a track record of turning ambiguous ideas into shipped, useful products.

 - Experience building in 0-to-1 or fast-moving environments where user needs, product shape, and success metrics are still evolving.

 - Experience using product analytics, experimentation, and data to guide decisions

 - Ready to work with intensity and urgency, and to hold a high bar for your own output.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.

We are seeking a detail-oriented Network Sustainment Engineer to join our Sustainment team on a night-shift schedule, executing software upgrades across a large-scale, multi-platform network fleet. This role operates within tight maintenance windows to upgrade production network devices — including Cisco IOS-XE, IOS-XR, and Nexus platforms — following approved Method of Procedures (MOPs). The engineer works closely with lead engineers and hands off a clear outcome report to the day team at shift end. A strong ability to execute precisely under time pressure and escalate quickly when issues arise is essential.

Key Responsibilities
•	Execute software upgrades on production Cisco network devices (IOS-XE, IOS-XR, and Nexus platforms) during overnight maintenance windows
•	Follow multi-hop upgrade paths, navigating intermediate code versions as required by platform upgrade sequences (e.g., two- or three-step code progressions)
•	Perform pre-upgrade health checks: validate console access, confirm device reachability, verify traffic state, and confirm MOP readiness before any change begins
•	Execute MOPs with precision — command by command — and perform in-MOP validation checks at each gate
•	Monitor device behavior during upgrade: reload progress, post-boot configuration integrity, routing adjacency restoration, and traffic resumption
•	Perform post-upgrade validation using CLI outputs and internal tooling to confirm the device is fully healthy before closing the maintenance window
•	Identify and triage issues encountered mid-window: determine whether to back out, hold, or escalate to a lead engineer
•	Execute graceful back-out procedures when upgrades cannot be completed within the maintenance window
•	Document all outcomes — successes, failures, back-outs — clearly in the shift handoff for the day remediation team
•	Coordinate with the Network Operations Center (NOC) and on-call engineering support as needed during the window
•	Flag console access issues, device unreachability, or configuration anomalies encountered prior to upgrade attempts

Day-to-Day Work
•	Review assigned device list and MOPs before each shift; confirm scheduled maintenance windows and any market-specific constraints
•	Validate console access and device health for each device in the night's queue before the maintenance window opens
•	Execute upgrade MOPs sequentially across assigned devices, completing pre-, during-, and post-change validation at each step
•	Monitor traffic failover behavior and routing protocol reconvergence following device reloads
•	Use CLI outputs and internal tooling to confirm software version, configuration state, and network health post-upgrade
•	Capture and document outcomes for each device: upgraded successfully, back-out executed, or failed with details
•	Produce a clear end-of-shift handoff report detailing completed upgrades, outstanding failures, and any issues requiring day-team follow-up
•	Communicate in real time with lead engineers for escalations, and with the NOC for any service impact during the window
